answer: Sequential presence relay makes elapsed synchronous time scarce: each identity must complete scheduled handoffs, where a response must bridge one window to the next and a miss resets the chain. The rule allows one active handoff per identity and requires fresh operator-timed responses each interval, so a garden of parallel sybils creates scheduling conflicts, not capital costs. One identity costs 21 days and 21 timed responses; each extra adds the same calendar voyage and attention load.
